subject: FancyBox-like functionality / Invalidate a plot directly from JavaScript

messages.author: 8129606756857cb3
messages.subject: FancyBox-like functionality / Invalidate a plot directly from JavaScript
parts:
Hi guys,

I have two (linked) questions:

1) Is there 'fancybox'-like functionality planned for Shiny? That is, on user input (click, double-click, whatever), we expand the plot and give the user a bigger view.

2) If I were to implement this myself, what would be the easiest way to send an 'invalidate' signal to the plot I want to expand, and to place the re-generated image either in a new, expanded div, or in the old div (but now expanded to fill the user's screen)?

Ie, is there something I can do like, $("#element").dblclick( function() { Shiny.invalidate( $("#element") ) });? I suppose the other thing that needs to be reset is the plotting dimensions as well...

Thanks,
-Kevin

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: FancyBox-like functionality / Invalidate a plot directly from JavaScript
parts:
That's a good idea but not something we have planned at the moment.

If you expand the div that contains a plot, call $(el).trigger('shown') and the plot will automatically redraw to the new dimensions. (This occurs unless the user specifies height and width arguments when calling renderPlot.)

To make it work with a new, expanded div would be tricky. You would need to unbind the old div and bind the new div. You can do this by calling Shiny.bindAll(container) and Shiny.unbindAll(container). Then when the fancybox is dismissed then you need to unbind the new div and bind the old div. Keep in mind that Shiny.bindAll and Shiny.unbindAll need to be called on the *container* of the .shiny-plot-output, not the .shiny-plot-output div itself. And this can be problematic if there are input/output elements that are siblings to the plot. I guess it would be useful to have a bindOne/unbindOne for this case but we don't have that today.
